skill.name: cursor-mem
skill.description: Access claude-mem from Cursor to search previous session records and save new observations through MCP tools.
skill.summary: Search and record shared claude-mem context across Cursor, Claude Code, Claude, and Codex workflows.
skill.author: Chachamaru127

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command, path-traversal, network, and obfuscation alerts are false positives from Markdown examples, inline MCP tool names, localhost checks, and Japanese prose. Confirmed risks remain around hidden local memory storage, a hidden plugin cache startup path, and broad Bash, Read, and MCP permissions. No prompt injection text was found in SKILL.md or examples.md.

remediation.issue: Broad Bash, Read, and wildcard MCP permissions are granted in the skill frontmatter.
remediation.suggestion: Limit allowed tools to the specific claude-mem MCP tools required for search and recording. Remove Bash and Read unless a workflow truly requires them.

remediation.issue: The shared memory database is stored in a hidden home-directory SQLite file.
remediation.suggestion: Document data retention, access controls, backup behavior, and secret-handling rules. Add redaction guidance before users store project or customer data.

remediation.issue: The troubleshooting command starts a worker from a hidden plugin cache path with a wildcard.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a pinned executable path or documented package command. Avoid wildcard execution from mutable cache directories.

remediation.issue: Shell troubleshooting commands are mixed into the skill usage instructions.
remediation.suggestion: Mark shell commands as manual setup steps and keep them separate from normal memory search and recording workflows.

content.user_title: Share Cursor Memory Across AI Coding Sessions
content.value_statement: AI coding sessions lose context when work moves between Cursor and Claude Code. This skill searches and records claude-mem entries so teams reuse decisions, patterns, and handoffs.
actual_capabilities: Search claude-mem records by keyword from Cursor through MCP tools.
Retrieve timelines, recent context, and individual observations.
Add observations for decisions, patterns, bugs, reviews, and handoffs.
Create memory entities and relations for structured project knowledge.
Share local memory records between Cursor and Claude Code workflows.
Guide Cursor MCP configuration for a claude-mem server.
limitations: Requires a working claude-mem MCP server and Cursor MCP configuration.
Does not encrypt, redact, or classify stored memory content by itself.
Search quality depends on clear tags and useful observation text.
Some troubleshooting steps may require manual local commands.

use_cases.title: Recover Prior Architecture Decisions
use_cases.description: Search earlier memory records before changing authentication, storage, or API design.

use_cases.title: Record Product Review Notes
use_cases.description: Save design judgments, review findings, and next steps for later implementation sessions.

use_cases.title: Transfer Context Between Tools
use_cases.description: Use Cursor to write handoff notes that Claude Code can read during implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Search a Past Decision
prompt_templates.prompt: Search claude-mem for why we chose the current authentication approach. Summarize the most relevant decision records.

prompt_templates.title: Record a Review Finding
prompt_templates.prompt: Record this review finding in claude-mem with source:cursor and type:review tags. Include the reason and affected component.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an Implementation Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a handoff note for the backend error-handling work. Include current status, required changes, risks, and useful tags.

prompt_templates.title: Build Context From Memory
prompt_templates.prompt: Search recent decisions, bugs, and patterns related to billing. Use the results to prepare a short implementation plan.

output_examples.output: The response lists the strongest matching memory records, explains the selected authentication approach, and names the tags that supported the match.
The response confirms the observation was saved with pattern, validation, source:cursor, and best-practice tags.

output_examples.input: Prepare a handoff for backend cleanup.
output_examples.output: The response creates a concise handoff entry with context, remaining work, risk notes, and suggested search terms for the next session.

best_practices: Tag every record with source, type, domain, and project terms.
Record why a decision was made, not only what changed.
Review memory content before storing secrets, credentials, or customer data.
anti_patterns: Do not store raw credentials, tokens, or private customer data.
Do not rely on memory search as the only project documentation source.
Do not use vague tags that make future searches hard to filter.

faq.question: What does this skill connect?
faq.answer: It connects Cursor workflows to claude-mem through MCP tools so memory records can be searched and written.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The documentation describes shared local memory that Cursor and Claude Code can both use.

faq.question: Where is memory stored?
faq.answer: The skill documents a local SQLite database under the user home directory for claude-mem records.

faq.question: Can it write new records?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes adding observations, creating entities, and creating relations through claude-mem MCP tools.

faq.question: Does it protect secrets automatically?
faq.answer: No. Users must avoid storing secrets or sensitive customer information unless their own controls allow it.

faq.question: What setup is required?
faq.answer: Users need a working claude-mem MCP server and a Cursor MCP configuration that points to the server command.
